purpose.statement: Make criteria, attempts, ownership, and current work visible while an agent is still working.
purpose.why: The larger goal is Expressive agent loops — make Barkpark Tasks give agents and users live, lock-grade progress instead of an opaque build phase. The concrete problem was that before this epic, proof appeared only at close and users could not see what criterion an agent was addressing or whether work was alive. Adding live stamps, pulses, events, a TUI progress strip, and dogfood wiring on the existing Tasks lifecycle was the correct intervention because the task record is already the lock and evidence authority, so surfacing its events avoids a parallel progress system. If omitted, agents can drift silently, users cannot distinguish stalled from active work, and close-time evidence arrives too late to steer.
